        "anchor": "stmt-lem-path-two-mesh",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a time horizon and a finite tree. For sufficiently small fixed mesh size $h$, the following comparisons hold.*\n\n*First, after events of probability smaller than every fixed inverse power of $n$ have been discarded on each actual forward marginal, the log density between actual and frozen paths, read in the tree-rooted direction, is at most $\\kappa(h)n+o(n)$ in absolute value, where $\\kappa(h)\\downarrow0$.*\n\n*Second, for spatial empirical tests one has the stronger entropy estimate $$H(Q\\mid P_h)\\le C_T hn+o(n),\n \\label{eq:path-mesh-entropy}$$ after the prescribed count and field truncations. Here $P_h$ is the frozen tree law. The law $Q$ is an admissible actual tree law, with the polynomial weights of [def:path-tree](#def:path-tree), possibly conditioned on an event of probability at least $n^{-M}$ for fixed $M$. The superpolynomial discards are made first on its original forward marginals. On the retained set its additional entropy relative to the stationary comparison is $o(n)$. Truncation errors vanish for this class in the successive order $n\\to\\infty$, cutoff $\\to\\infty$ at fixed $h$, then $h\\downarrow0$. For use at a fixed $h$ the cutoff is chosen so that its entropy error is at most $hn$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-thm-path-calculus",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $0<\\beta<1$, a finite tree, a finite collection of words and recipes, and fixed caps on its diagonal labels. Dimension is taken to infinity before any recipe accuracy, mesh, cap, or time limit. The following assertions hold in the typicality convention of [def:path-tree](#def:path-tree).*\n\n1.  *Stationary recipe overlaps, normalized traces, and joint empirical averages have deterministic limits. The completion of one-state recipes for the limiting inner product is a separable real Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$. Conditional means of path recipes at a chosen endpoint have approximations in $\\mathcal H$. The same stationary predictors work on actual conditional trees: centered copies sharing that endpoint have vanishing spatial pair overlaps.*\n\n2.  *If $u_n$ is measurable at that endpoint, $\\mathbb E\\left\\lVert u_n\\right\\rVert^2\\le C$, $\\left\\lVert u_n\\right\\rVert\\le n^M$, and $$\\mathbb E|u_n^tb_n|^2\\longrightarrow0\n     \\quad\\text{for every endpoint recipe }b_n,\n     \\label{eq:path-hidden}$$ then $u_n$ is orthogonal in this same squared sense to all bounded path recipe vectors. Multiplication by bounded path words preserves this assertion, with the transpose placed on the other vector as necessary. Such vectors will be called *hidden*.*\n\n3.  *On the complement of visible dyads, joint limiting word inner products of hidden vectors are represented on a Hilbert space with $J/\\beta=s=\\ell+\\ell^*$ and $$\\ell^*D\\ell=\\tau(D)I.\n     \\label{eq:path-creation}$$ Here $\\tau$ is the limiting spatial state on the diagonal algebra. The representation retains an arbitrary bounded base action of every diagonal, including types of zero limiting proportion. A single representation suffices for all the finitely many vectors and words on the fixed tree. No compatible choice between different trees is asserted.*\n\n4.  *Normalized traces are given by complete noncrossing contractions. For a word $Q$, let $\\Delta(Q)$ be its complete contraction with the outer diagonal unaveraged. Then $$\\max_i|Q_{ii}-\\Delta(Q)_i|\\longrightarrow0,\n     \\qquad \\max_{i\\ne j}|Q_{ij}|\\longrightarrow0.\n     \\label{eq:path-entry-prediction}$$ For two bounded path matrices, $$Q\\circ R=D_{\\Delta(Q)\\Delta(R)}+V+o_{\\mathrm{op}}(1),\n     \\label{eq:path-hadamard}$$ where $V$ is in the operator-norm closure of bounded visible dyads.*\n\n5.  *Bounded clipped likelihood labels admit tracial $L^2$ approximations by fixed finite smooth multitime calculations satisfying the mixed-slot bounds of [lem:path-mixed-tensors](#lem:path-mixed-tensors), with observation times inside their path span. One-sided endpoint approximations are allowed. When only spin observations are used, the likelihood is the flip-rate likelihood. Predictors of these labels mean predictors of these tracial approximants in successive limits, with the same cap.*\n\n6.  *Smooth site-recipe difference matrices, their bounded products, and matrices with column $j$ evaluated at $x^j$ belong to the same operator closure. Their off-diagonal difference entries vanish uniformly. Conditional expected derivative matrices have the stronger pointwise truncation property in [lem:path-conditional-derivative](#lem:path-conditional-derivative) for those fixed smooth calculations. Their opened derivative terms reduce to path matrices by [prop:path-opened-derivative](#prop:path-opened-derivative).*\n\n*For two independent stationary roots in the same disorder, the limiting spin, field, and bounded likelihood histories at a uniformly sampled site are independent copies. This last assertion is restricted to these spin-generated histories. It is not asserted for arbitrary noncentered recipes or recipes sharing site seeds.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal A$ be a class of uniformly bounded finite matrix expressions, closed under products, transposes, Hadamard products, and multiplication by its bounded diagonal labels.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-path-opened-derivative",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a smooth multitime calculation as in [lem:path-mixed-tensors](#lem:path-mixed-tensors), a finite causal tree, common Duhamel and likelihood truncations from [lem:path-conditional-derivative](#lem:path-conditional-derivative), and the tensor approximations of [lem:path-increment-approximation](#lem:path-increment-approximation). Require every linear-query edge of the calculation and every opened $K$ edge to belong to the admitted path-matrix algebra, with its entry predictions, and require all bounded coefficient labels to be admitted path labels. In particular, the calculation values are admitted path recipes; the likelihood calculations above use $J$ and $J\\circ J$ as their query matrices. The broader class of arbitrary bounded-operator query maps in [lem:path-mixed-tensors](#lem:path-mixed-tensors) is not asserted to have this closure. After ordinary conditional expectations are opened on their specified causal branches, every remaining derivative contraction is a bounded path matrix up to successive operator-norm errors. It has vanishing off-diagonal maximum and the Hadamard and diagonal predictions of [lem:path-hadamard](#lem:path-hadamard). The network errors have the typical, weighted and integrated-parameter meaning of [def:path-tree](#def:path-tree).         "anchor": "stmt-thm-row-projected-moments",
        "exact_quote": "For each fixed real $r$ and each $\\varepsilon>0$, there is $d_0=d_0(r,\\varepsilon)$ such that, for every fixed $d\\ge d_0$ and every deterministic mask $M$, outside a disorder event of probability tending to zero there is a set $B_{n,d,M}$ satisfying $$\\mu(B_{n,d,M})\\le e^{-c n},\\qquad\n \\max_i\\mathbb E_x\\bigl[(A_{i,x}^M(X_d))^r\\bigr]\n       \\le e^{\\varepsilon d}+o_n(1)\n \\quad(x\\notin B_{n,d,M}).\n \\label{eq:row-moment-quantified}$$ Here $c>0$ can depend on the fixed $d,r,\\varepsilon$, but the estimates in the proof are uniform in the deterministic mask. Thus the notation $e^{o_r(d)}$ for these moments always means dimension first and then $d\\to\\infty$. For $0\\le r\\le1$ the upper bound $1$ follows directly from Jensen’s inequality. Negative $r$ in [eq:row-moment-quantified](#eq:row-moment-quantified) refers to the unrestricted positive likelihood, not to a likelihood multiplied by a cutoff indicator.*\n\n*The theorem also holds in its integrated form: if $M=M_\\alpha$ ranges over a deterministic measurable family with a finite measure on its parameter space, the good disorder event can be chosen so that the *integrated* Gibbs mass of the exceptional starts is exponentially small. This includes masks determined by simplex times in a fixed finite path expansion and the independent Poisson schedules used below. It does not assert a simultaneous bound for a mask selected to maximize an error after seeing the disorder.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-row-hilbert-representation",
        "exact_quote": "After subsequence extraction, a replicated array of the lists in [eq:row-bridge-list](#eq:row-bridge-list) has the following representation. Conditional on a directing variable $\\mathcal D$, each branch draws independently its self-Gram matrix $Q$, its bracket data, and a list of vectors $r_\\alpha$ in one separable real Hilbert space. Cross-Grams between distinct branches are $\\left\\langle r_\\alpha,r'_\\gamma\\right\\rangle$, and $Q-(\\left\\langle r_\\alpha,r_\\gamma\\right\\rangle)_{\\alpha,\\gamma}$ is positive semidefinite. Include the factor $\\beta$ in the vectors. Conditional on these data, the row projections have the form $$g(r_\\alpha)+\\xi_\\alpha,\n \\label{eq:row-shared-private}$$ where $g$ is one common isonormal process and, independently on each branch, $\\xi$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $Q-(\\left\\langle r_\\alpha,r_\\gamma\\right\\rangle)$. Conditional averages in this representation integrate one branch and its coins with $\\mathcal D,g$ held fixed.",
        "source_id": "PM-227.4"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-row-overlap-norm",
        "exact_quote": "If $r,r'$ are independent with the same law in a separable Hilbert space and $|\\left\\langle r,r'\\right\\rangle|\\le\\delta$ almost surely, then $\\left\\lVert r\\right\\rVert^2\\le\\delta$ almost surely. The same assertion holds conditionally on a directing variable.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-hidden-marked-spine",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an opened, capped derivative history of one smooth multitime label. Suppose it has an entering derivative index, at least one branch differentiating that label, and one derivative index continuing to a later factor. Its temporal derivative tree has a unique path between the entering and continuing indices. Absorb the part before its first label attachment into the incoming propagation matrix, and retain the part after its last attachment as a subsequent bounded propagation. Let $M$ be the matrix arriving at the first attachment, with label site as row and derivative index as column.*\n\n*If $\\Phi(M)$ is the matrix after the intervening history, then, in the finite-tree comparison, $$\\label{eq:hidden-marked-spine-bound}\n \\left\\lVert \\Phi(M)\\right\\rVert_{\\mathrm{HS}}\n \\leq C\\left\\lVert \\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}(M)\\right\\rVert+o(1)\\left\\lVert M\\right\\rVert_{\\mathrm{HS}}.$$ Here $C$ depends on the fixed circuit and capped history. All memory copies and all mixed differences of the label are included in this history. The estimate does not replace a mixed label tensor by an ordinary first Jacobian.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "Fix a logarithmic horizon, a polynomial envelope, and a common constant $C_P$ in the defective trajectory Poincaré bound [eq:cutoff-trajectory-poincare](#eq:cutoff-trajectory-poincare), with arbitrarily prescribed inverse-power accuracy. Suppose also that either $p_b$ is a fixed nondegenerate finite linear combination of concentrating visible exact test gradients, or there is a subsequent block with $N_{b+D}\\le R N_b$ for a fixed finite $R$.         "anchor": "stmt-rcut-prop-uniform-gap",
        "exact_quote": "For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly over $J\\in\\mathcal E_n$, $s\\in[0,1]$, and $\\theta\\in\\mathbb R^n$, let $$\\nu_{s,\\theta}(x)\\propto\n \\exp\\left(\\frac s2x^{\\mathsf T}Jx+\\theta\\cdot x\\right).$$ Its rate-one-per-site heat-bath generator has spectral gap at least $$\\kappa_\\beta=\\frac{1-2\\beta}{2}>0.$$ Moreover, $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Var}}_{\\nu_{s,\\theta}}(f)\n \\le\\kappa_\\beta^{-1}\\sum_i\n       \\nu_{s,\\theta}[v_i(d_i f)^2],\n \\qquad\n \\|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Cov}}_{\\nu_{s,\\theta}}(X)\\|\\le\\kappa_\\beta^{-1}.\n \\label{rcut:eq:uniform-gap-covariance}$$",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Gaussian SK Gibbs law** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Independently for $i<j$, choose $J_{ij}\sim N(0,\beta^2/n)$, set $J_{ji}=J_{ij}$ and $J_{ii}=0$, and put $$\mu_J(x)=Z_J^{-1}\exp\!\left(\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Jx\right).$$
- **Discrete half-difference** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Define the half-difference $$d_i f(x)=\frac{f(x^{i,+})-f(x^{i,-})}{2}.$$
- **Conditional spin labels** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Writing the conditional mean, conditional variance, and twice the flip rate as $$m_i(x)=\tanh((Jx)_i),\qquad v_i(x)=1-m_i(x)^2,\qquad w_i(x)=1-x_i m_i(x),$$
- **Unscaled conditional-covariance form** ([source](#pm-h-12)): We define the unscaled form for any full-support law $Q$ on the cube by conditional covariance: $$\mathcal E_Q(f,g) =\sum_i \mathbb E_Q\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}_Q(f,g\mid X_{-i}),\qquad \mathcal E_Q(f)=\mathcal E_Q(f,f).$$
- **Exact discrete product and commutation identities** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Differentiating the generator later will require the exact product rule, including its quadratic correction, and the commutation identities $$\begin{aligned} d_i(fg)&=f\,d_i g+g\,d_i f-2x_i\,d_i f\,d_i g, \label{eq:model-product}\\ d_i d_jf&=d_jd_if,\qquad d_i^2f=0. \label{eq:model-commute} \end{aligned}$$
- **Worst-start total-variation distances** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Set $$d_n(t)=\max_{x\in\Omega_n}\left\lVert S_t(x,\cdot)-\mu\right\rVert_{\mathop{\mathrm{TV}}}, \qquad d_n^{\rm disc}(k)=\max_{x\in\Omega_n}\left\lVert P^k(x,\cdot)-\mu\right\rVert_{\mathop{\mathrm{TV}}}.$$
- **Changed-law energy and entropy** ([source](#sec:static)): Set $$D_P(Q)=\mathcal E_P\bigl(\sqrt{Q/P}\bigr),\qquad H_P(Q)=\sum_x Q(x)\log\frac{Q(x)}{P(x)}.$$
- **Stable-field diagnostics** ([source](#pm-h-17)): We refer to them, together with $\left\lVert M\right\rVert\le K$, as the deterministic diagnostics.
- **Mixed-slot tensor norm** ([source](#pm-h-23)): For a nonempty $I\subseteq[m]$ define $$(T_IF)_{i,(j_a:a\in I)} =\prod_{a\in I}d_{j_a}^{(a)}F_i, \qquad C_I(F)=\sup_{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(m)}} \left\lVert T_IF\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}. \label{eq:path-mixed-norm}$$
- **Admissible finite tree tests** ([source](#stmt-def-path-tree)): A stationary path tree has finitely many edges of fixed finite lengths. Choose a root state with law $\mu$ and run independent ordinary heat-bath paths outwards along the edges. Reversibility permits an edge to be read in either direction. A nonstationary tree is obtained from a forward path whose initial density $h$ satisfies $\log\left\lVert h\right\rVert_\infty=o(n)$, and by making finitely many conditional copies of portions at a shared *single endpoint*, using their actual conditional laws. No new branch is conditioned on both of its endpoints. A test has a fixed finite list of times and a fixed polynomial bound $n^M$. Its weight $W_n$ satisfies $\|W_n\|\le n^M$ and $\mathbb E\|W_n\|\le C$. A bounded test assertion is called typical if it holds in expectation with every such weight, on disorder events of probability tending to one. One may pass to subsequences and successive finite approximations. The exponent $M$, all times, the tree, and each approximation are fixed before $n\to\infty$.
- **Recipe** ([source](#pm-h-27)): A *recipe* is a finite calculation from these inputs, using multiplication by $J$, finite linear combinations, and bounded smooth componentwise functions with bounded derivatives.
- **Path label** ([source](#pm-h-27)): A *path label* is a bounded site function obtained from such a finite calculation, from a capped elementary likelihood, or from a successive tracial approximation of either.
- **Path matrix and visible dyads** ([source](#pm-h-27)): A *path matrix* is a fixed word, or a finite linear combination of words, in $J$ and the corresponding diagonal labels. The class also contains bounded finite-rank dyads of path recipe vectors and their successive operator-norm limits. We call these dyads *visible*.
- **Hidden endpoint vector** ([source](#sec:hidden)): An endpoint vector $u$ is *hidden* if $$\mathbb E\left\lvert u^t B\right\rvert^2\longrightarrow0$$ for every fixed recipe vector $B$ at that endpoint.
- **Projected masked row likelihood** ([source](#pm-h-35)): Put $$A_{i,x}^M(y)=\mathbb E_x[\ell_i^M\mid X_d=y]. \label{eq:row-projection}$$
- **Spin spectral measure** ([source](#pm-h-41)): Let $E_n(\,\mathrm du)$ be the spectral resolution of $-L$ on $L^2(\mu)$, and encode the spin coordinates by the positive matrix-valued measure $$\mathsf M_n(\,\mathrm du)_{ij} =\left\langle x_i,E_n(\,\mathrm du)x_j\right\rangle_\mu, \qquad \rho_n(\,\mathrm du)=\frac1n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\mathsf M_n(\,\mathrm du).$$
- **Spin edge and response kernel** ([source](#pm-h-41)): Set $$\lambda_{\rm sp}=\inf\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\rho>0, \qquad R(t)=-C'(t)=\int u e^{-ut}\rho(\,\mathrm du).$$
- **Ordinary and weighted visible metrics** ([source](#pm-h-49)): For stationary vector fields put $$\label{eq:exact-metrics} \left\langle p,q\right\rangle_0=\mathbb E_\mu p^{\mathsf T}q, \qquad \left\langle p,q\right\rangle_v=\mathbb E_\mu p^{\mathsf T}D_vq, \qquad \mathfrak d(p)=\mathbb E_\mu\sum_{i,j}v_j\left\lvert d_jp_i\right\rvert^2.$$
- **Covariance test potential** ([source](#pm-h-49)): For a smooth bounded scaled vector recipe $B$ and $\delta>0$, define $$\label{eq:exact-potential} f_{B,\delta} =\delta^{-1}\left\{x^{\mathsf T}S_\delta B -S_\delta\bigl[(S_\delta x)^{\mathsf T}B\bigr]\right\}.$$
- **Exact visible spaces** ([source](#stmt-def-exact-spaces)): Let $\mathcal X$ be the closure in $\mathcal H$ of the linear span of $$K_tdf_{B,\delta},\qquad t\ge0,\quad\delta>0, \quad B\text{ a smooth bounded scaled recipe}.$$ Let $\mathcal X_v$ be the closure of the same span in $\mathcal H_v$. Equivalently, countable dense recipe, time, and accuracy sets may be used.
- **Equilibrium cutoff rate** ([source](#stmt-thm-exact-sector)): In particular the number $$\label{eq:exact-lambda} \lambda =\min\left\{\lambda_{\rm sp},\inf\mathop{\mathrm{spec}}(\mathcal A_v)\right\} \quad\text{satisfies}\quad 0<\lambda\le\lambda_{\rm sp}\le(1-\beta)^2.$$
- **Scalar Gaussian variational functional** ([source](#rcut:eq:variational)): For measurable real $b$ and nonnegative $r$ with $\langle b^2+r^2\rangle=1$, define $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal V_\beta(b,r) ={}&\langle D(b^2+r^2)\rangle +\langle bh\rangle\langle bv\rangle +\langle b\rangle\langle bhv\rangle -\beta^2\langle b\rangle\langle bv\rangle \notag\\ &+2\beta^2\langle b\rangle\langle bmv\rangle +\beta^2\langle b(h)K_0(h,h_*)b(h_*)\rangle_{h,h_*} \notag\\ &+\beta\left\langle r(h) \sqrt{\left\langle(v(h)+v(h_*))^2r(h_*)^2\right\rangle_* +\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_{h_*}\bigl((v(h)+v(h_*))b(h_*)\bigr)} \right\rangle. \label{rcut:eq:variational} \end{aligned}$$

## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-import-gap** [claim](#stmt-thm-input-gap) / [proof](#pm-h-13): Import the all-functions equilibrium Poincaré inequality with its unscaled normalization. -> Positive equilibrium heat-bath gap.
- **step-jump-moments** [claim](#stmt-lem-input-mgf) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-input-mgf): Apply the exponential jump compensator to the backward martingale. -> Terminal exponential moments and variance.
- **step-clock-array-transfer** [claim](#stmt-lem-input-clock) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-trapezoid-3): Use local clock limits and a fixed finite signed approximation by Gaussian translates. -> Uniform binomial-average convergence.
- **step-independent-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-prop-model-independent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-model-independent): Bound the product density above and distinguish magnetization below. -> Independent-spin cutoff.
- **step-arbitrary-law-mean** [claim](#stmt-lem-stat-mean) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-stat-mean): Extend residual identities, select consecutive small residuals using first moments, and compare with the stable root. -> Arbitrary-law spin-mean control.
- **step-posterior-cavity-gaps** [claim](#stmt-prop-stat-posterior-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-stat-posterior-gap): Create large fields, control second-stage curvature, and condition the remaining observation experiment to recover first-stage gaps. -> Common posterior and cavity gaps with a test-independent stop.
- **step-field-subset-tails** [claim](#stmt-lem-stat-field-tails) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-stat-field-tails): Prove planted Gaussian subset tails and transfer them through the partition function to fixed disorder. -> Simultaneous field subset tails including cavities.
- **step-entropy-energy** [claim](#stmt-thm-stat-entropy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-stat-entropy): Combine stopped drift energy, product tensorization, and weighted field-tail absorption. -> Defective entropy-energy inequality.
- **step-fixed-density** [claim](#stmt-prop-stat-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-stat-density): Retain the defect in hypercontractivity and balance it against the prescribed fixed horizon. -> Fixed-time specific log-density estimate.
- **step-vector-generator** [claim](#stmt-prop-path-gradient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-path-gradient): Differentiate the scalar generator using the exact discrete product rule and expand the variance-retaining coefficients. -> Exact vector intertwining and coefficient bounds.
- **step-vector-tails** [claim](#stmt-prop-path-rough) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-path-rough): Absorb first-order terms in the square evolution, represent row likelihoods, and truncate the factorial insertion expansion. -> All-vector propagation and common likelihood tails.
- **step-tensor-products** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-tensor-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-tensor-product): Restrict row tensor products by equality isometries and use Schur bounds for repeated squares. -> Dimension-independent tensor product estimates.
- **step-mixed-slots** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-mixed-tensors) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-mixed-tensors): Use corner increments, a covering expansion, and a repeated-increment remainder. -> Uniform mixed-slot operator budgets.
- **step-conditional-derivatives** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-conditional-derivative) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-conditional-derivative): Eliminate leaves with all mixed slots retained and replace each evolving operator by common linear truncations. -> Uniform conditional derivative and row-weighted error bounds.
- **step-tree-transfer** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-tree-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-tree-transfer): Remove reverse joining states with small density denominators before comparing the retained tree densities. -> Weighted and integrated transfer of exponential rarity.
- **step-frozen-comparisons** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-two-mesh) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-two-mesh): Separate absolute log-density control from quadratic log-likelihood entropy control and make discards on original forward marginals. -> Density and entropy comparisons with distinct error scales.
- **step-product-concentration** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-product): Prove a Bernoulli entropy estimate by convexity, tensorize, and optimize the entropy variational bound. -> Product concentration and expectation transfer.
- **step-smooth-simulations** [claim](#stmt-prop-path-simulation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-path-simulation): Use actual-law and autonomous frozen-law telescopes with a common semigroup reference, then smooth in backward nested order. -> Finite smooth simulation and replicated endpoint approximation.
- **step-finite-regression** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-regression) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-regression): Plant the initial spin and iteratively condition Gaussian matrix columns, omitting small query residuals before inversion. -> Deterministic empirical limits and independent compressed Gaussian remainder.
- **step-endpoint-prediction** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-prediction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-prediction): Complete deterministic Gram limits, approximate conditional means using seed averages, and apply replicated Bessel estimates. -> Recipe Hilbert space, endpoint predictors, and hidden orthogonality.
- **step-likelihood-labels** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-likelihood-approximation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-likelihood-approximation): Expand flip scores, freeze bounded integrands, retain mixed queries, and cap the score using a finite sign decomposition. -> Tracial likelihood approximants with controlled mixed tensors.
- **step-fock-norm** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-fock-norm) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-fock-norm): Count Wick diagrams for positive types, retain rare coordinate blocks, remove polynomial norm losses by powers, and concentrate. -> Fixed-word Fock norm domination retaining rare base actions.
- **step-sparse-labels** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-sparse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-sparse): Pay the finite modification entropy from a fixed Gaussian failure rate before selecting a separate finer density mesh. -> Simultaneous comparison for sparse adaptive label changes.
- **step-compressed-words** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-compressed) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-compressed): Complete the compressed Gaussian matrix independently, remove queried dyads in hidden tests, and extend the positive word functional. -> Joint hidden-word representation on a fixed tree.
- **step-hadamard** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-hadamard) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-hadamard): Prove uniform entry predictions, separate diffuse and large-coordinate tests, and identify the visible mean of off-diagonal products. -> Diagonal prediction and Hadamard operator reduction.
- **step-difference-closure** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-difference-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-difference-closure): Induct through smooth difference expansions and exact column-flip recursions using Hadamard closure. -> Static smooth difference and column-flip closure.
- **step-increment-polynomials** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-increment-approximation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-increment-approximation): Approximate remainder coefficients on the compact increment box while retaining repeated factors controlling operator error. -> Finite equality-network tensor polynomials.
- **step-network-reduction** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-directed-network) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-directed-network): Apply series and parallel reductions and pinch safe internal edges using uniform off-diagonal smallness. -> Path-matrix contraction with operator-small error.
- **step-opened-derivatives** [claim](#stmt-prop-path-opened-derivative) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-path-opened-derivative): Remove uniform tensor and propagation errors, glue temporal and spatial derivative trees, and reduce the opened network. -> Dynamic derivative closure on the specified causal trees.
- **step-independent-roots** [claim](#stmt-lem-path-two-root) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-two-root): Plant independent spins, show cross-query overlaps vanish by root inversion, and propagate independent Gaussian innovations. -> Product limiting site histories for independent equilibrium roots.
- **step-complete-path-calculus** [claim](#stmt-thm-path-calculus) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-path-two-root-2): Assemble empirical, prediction, likelihood, operator, derivative, and restricted independent-root comparisons under successive fixed approximations. -> Finite-tree Gaussian calculus with its precise typicality convention.
- **step-row-integrability** [claim](#stmt-lem-row-uniform-integrability) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-uniform-integrability): Bound raw likelihood moments, control the forced coin through linear jump moments, and use conditional Jensen and replicated averages. -> Fixed-time uniform integrability for conditional row averages.
- **step-shared-private-representation** [claim](#stmt-lem-row-hilbert-representation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-hilbert-representation): Extract principal coordinates and self-Grams of conditionally independent bridge lists, then realize the Gaussian covariance split. -> Shared isonormal and private Gaussian branch representation.
- **step-overlap-to-norm** [claim](#stmt-lem-row-overlap-norm) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-overlap-norm): Use continuity around a support point and separability to contradict any excessive norm. -> Almost-sure bound for shared prefix score norms.
- **step-chronological-gaussian** [claim](#stmt-lem-row-adapted-gaussian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-adapted-gaussian): Condition on corrected covariance data and integrate scores in the order before which their signs are chosen. -> Near-unity-power prefix moment bounds.
- **step-projected-row-moments** [claim](#stmt-thm-row-projected-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-adapted-gaussian-2): Use a terminal buffer to suppress shared prefix scores, apply conditional Hölder, and remove schedules through Jensen and raw higher moments. -> Dimension-first subexponential projected moments and integrated exceptional-start control.
- **step-stationary-row-predictors** [claim](#stmt-cor-row-stationary-predictors) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-row-stationary-predictors): Condition on endpoints, use Jensen, and bound exceptional starts with a higher raw moment. -> Right predictor subexponential moments and left predictor boundedness.
- **step-spin-renewal** [claim](#stmt-prop-spin-spectrum) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-spin-spectrum): Derive positive trunk convolution identities, bound transforms by polynomial domination, and test covariance mass near the matrix spectral edge. -> Spin-edge bound and strict renewal inequalities.
- **step-centered-trace-errors** [claim](#stmt-lem-hidden-small-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hidden-small-trace): Project the terminal visible part, expand Fock cuts, and replicate the centered pure side on a single star. -> Small-trace replacement within doubly centered bilinear tests.
- **step-marked-derivative** [claim](#stmt-lem-hidden-marked-spine) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hidden-marked-spine): Pull side branches into a bounded row tensor, pinch marked-path segments, and retain the complete label derivative network. -> Marked-history Hilbert–Schmidt estimate.
- **step-two-ended-averaging** [claim](#stmt-lem-hidden-averaging) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hidden-marked-spine-2): Use martingale covariance, classify the derivative's first destination, and cancel through backward centering or a nonempty Wick prefix. -> Two-ended Wick averaging in hidden bilinear tests.
- **step-hidden-propagation** [claim](#stmt-thm-hidden-propagation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hidden-marked-spine-3): Truncate paths, average labels, remove likelihood annuli in nested order, and sum positive renewal majorants with weighted-density control. -> Hidden propagation below the spin edge.
- **step-visible-smoothing** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-smoothing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-smoothing): Retain variance weights in the square evolution and treat the vector generator as a relatively bounded perturbation of componentwise heat flow. -> Compatible strongly continuous semigroups and ordinary analytic smoothing.
- **step-exact-visible-generator** [claim](#stmt-thm-exact-sector) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-exact-sector): Pass the finite exact-gradient self-adjoint pairing to the weighted closure and apply the spectral theorem. -> Deterministic weighted exact generator and cutoff-rate definition.
- **step-exact-saturation** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-saturation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-saturation): Test the orthogonal remainder using covariance potentials and the own-spin jump-weight isometry. -> Saturation of the weighted exact sector.
- **step-coefficient-transport** [claim](#stmt-prop-exact-transport) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-exact-transport): Test finite recipe projections before rough scalar multiplication and use replicated prediction to remove the complement. -> Tensor-product transport with no scalar differentiation.
- **step-good-comparison-times** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-good-times) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-good-times): Tilt by terminal gradient energy and combine integrated rough dissipation with the reverse path entropy budget. -> Selected times with simultaneous Hessian and reverse Hellinger bounds.
- **step-adjoint-annihilation** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-adjoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-adjoints): Multiply stationary adjoint tests by visible contractions and estimate the nonstationary remainder through complementary budgets. -> Scalar-square-mean adjoint annihilation.
- **step-strong-form-closure** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-form-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-form-closure): Smooth in the componentwise form norm, approximate by finite recipes, and use strong derivative density to test the full curl norm. -> Strong representatives with vanishing weighted curl and own-spin derivative.
- **step-own-spin-removal** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-own-spin) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-own-spin): Compare conditional pair laws with the uncoupled product law while retaining conditional variance factors. -> Own-spin-independent representatives preserving vanishing curl.
- **step-no-defect** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-no-defect) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-no-defect): Transport the optimized residual cost using posterior gaps and concavity of pair weights, then apply the product Fourier bound. -> Weighted distance-to-gradients controlled by curl.
- **step-visible-closedness** [claim](#stmt-prop-exact-closedness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-exact-closedness): Apply strong closure, own-spin removal, and the observation inequality to each deterministic scalar contraction, then saturate. -> Weighted exactness of the vector factor of the random projection.
- **step-unweighted-upgrade** [claim](#stmt-lem-exact-upgrade) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-exact-upgrade): Separate the diagonal differential semigroup and convolve its ordinary decay with the weighted multiplication estimate. -> Unweighted exact-sector decay with strict rate slack.
- **step-spectrum-isolation** [claim](#stmt-prop-exact-isolation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-exact-isolation): Represent weakly null norm witnesses by genuinely hidden sequences, bound the essential norm, and identify spectral projections through the dense embedding. -> Isolated slow modes and compatible weighted and ordinary projections.
- **step-uniform-block** [claim](#stmt-prop-cutoff-block) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cutoff-block): Restart on a fixed interval, prove limiting strict contraction, normalize only above an inverse-polynomial threshold, and use deterministic diagonal selection for fixed burn-in. -> Uniform block contraction over starts, tests, and allowed origins.
- **step-logarithmic-propagation** [claim](#stmt-prop-cutoff-gradient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cutoff-gradient): Iterate the common block and sum its contracting additive errors; handle bounded leftover intervals by rough propagation. -> Logarithmic propagation and linear gradient envelopes.
- **step-cube-oscillation** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-oscillation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-oscillation): Extend multilinearly and integrate the bounded Euclidean gradient along vertex-to-vertex segments. -> Oscillation bound for cube observables.
- **step-upper-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-upper) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-upper): Select a late time from the martingale energy budget, recover unweighted energy using field tails, and propagate back before applying oscillation. -> Worst-start upper cutoff.
- **step-spin-lower** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-spin-lower) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-spin-lower): Use a fixed positive amount of spectral mass near the edge to select a starting configuration and distinguish its linear mean. -> Lower cutoff when the spin edge determines the rate.
- **step-slow-coefficient-alignment** [claim](#stmt-prop-cutoff-coefficients) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cutoff-coefficients): Transport the slow mean, bound coefficient fluctuations with coarse recipes, choose the block, and only then refine reporting recipes. -> Uniform slow mean and fluctuation alignment.
- **step-preparation-bounds** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-preparation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-preparation): Compare marked-attempt likelihoods and differentiate the perturbed generator to obtain a common rough gradient bound. -> Prepared-law density and common Poincaré estimates.
- **step-slow-cone** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-cone) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-cone): Iterate the coefficient alignment within a cone and retain a predetermined inverse-polynomial norm threshold. -> A slow mean coefficient and small reconstruction residual.
- **step-mean-ball** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-jacobian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-jacobian): Differentiate preparation expectations by Duhamel, use short-time continuity, and lift straight target segments by the inverse Jacobian. -> Ball of attainable terminal means.
- **step-visible-lower** [claim](#stmt-lem-cutoff-visible-lower) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cutoff-visible-lower): Choose a diverging attainable mean, compare bounded variances, and use convexity to select a deterministic start. -> Lower cutoff for an isolated visible rate.
- **step-continuous-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-thm-cutoff-continuous) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-cutoff-continuous): Combine the upper bound with the exhaustive spin-edge and slower-visible alternatives. -> Continuous-time high-temperature cutoff.
- **step-attempt-clock-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-prop-cutoff-clock) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cutoff-clock): Transfer the lower side by Poisson concentration and the upper side by fixed holding and shifted-array clock comparison. -> Cutoff in attempted uniform-site updates.
- **step-main-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cutoff-clock): Combine the independent endpoint with the positive-temperature continuous theorem and its attempt-clock transfer. -> The main worst-start cutoff theorem.
- **step-restricted-gaussian-facts** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-gaussian-facts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-gaussian-facts): Use Gaussian rotation for exponential moments and interpolation for expected suprema. -> Gaussian concentration and comparison estimates.
- **step-restricted-disorder** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-good-disorder) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-good-disorder): Add a Gaussian diagonal for norm comparison and combine row-square and entry tails. -> Common good-disorder norm and entry controls.
- **step-two-spin** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-two-spin) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-two-spin): Factor conditional variances, identify the nonnegative expansion, and charge the analytic cubic remainder to one-site energies. -> Uniform signed two-spin inequality.
- **step-uniform-scaled-gap** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-uniform-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-uniform-gap): Sum signed pair inequalities and bound the interaction and squared-interaction matrices by their norms. -> Gap and covariance uniform over fields and interaction scales.
- **step-restricted-entropy** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-entropy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-entropy): Interpolate to product Gaussian posteriors, bound covariance by entropy, tensorize, and remove the observation by conditioning. -> Entropy inequality and point-start entropy decay.
- **step-gradient-algebra** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-gradient-algebra) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-gradient-algebra): Differentiate the unweighted gradient energy, retain variance factors in field differences, and complete pairwise squares. -> Pointwise quadratic-form dissipation bound.
- **step-square-replacement** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-comp-square-replacement) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-comp-square-replacement): Truncate squares for the operator estimate, approximate continuous kernels, and remove the active row before field-dependent diagonal concentration. -> Exponentially reliable weighted square replacement.
- **step-bin-gaussian** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-comp-bin-gaussian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-comp-bin-gaussian): Separate constant-bin and zero-sum blocks, verify increment domination, and concentrate the full residual supremum. -> Conditional Gaussian variational majorant.
- **step-planted-comparison** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-planted-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-comp-bin-gaussian-2): Replace squares, discretize fields, preserve normalization through bin-mass rescaling, and extend concentrated net bounds to all parameters. -> Exponential planted quadratic-form control.
- **step-annealed-transfer** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-annealed-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-annealed-transfer): Use sign conjugation for the exceptional numerator and concentration plus a second moment for the partition denominator. -> Exponentially small quenched Gibbs exceptional mass.
- **step-kernel-remainder** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-kernel): Expand the compactified kernel into positive rank terms and sum the residual diagonal. -> Nonnegative remainder and coherent kernel bound.
- **step-trapezoidal-certificate** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-trapezoid) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-trapezoid): Periodize the strip-holomorphic integrand and bound Fourier coefficients by shifted contours. -> Whole-line quadrature error estimate.
- **step-scalar-moment-certificate** [claim](#stmt-rcut-tab-scalar-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-trapezoid-2): Combine strip and tail errors, outward integer arithmetic, normalized moment transfer, and perturbation of the means in the mixed coefficient. -> Strict scalar moment enclosures.
- **step-diagonal-envelope** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-envelope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-envelope): Reduce to the endpoint temperature by positivity and bound the field dependence by quadratic envelopes. -> Uniform scalar diagonal coefficient bound.
- **step-coherent-form** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-coherent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-coherent): Center the test function, bound the coherent kernel, and certify positive slack against the mixed coefficient throughout the interval. -> Uniform coherent quadratic-form bound.
- **step-scalar-variational-gap** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-scalar-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-scalar-coherent-2): Apply field-dependent Young separation and add the diagonal envelope and coherent allowance. -> Strict scalar variational gap.
- **step-typical-gradient** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-typical-gradient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-typical-gradient): Use the global rough estimate at smaller temperatures and the planted variational gap plus annealed transfer otherwise. -> Typical-state gradient contraction with an exponentially small bad set.
- **step-feynman-kac** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-feynman-kac) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-feynman-kac): Run the semigroup parameter backward along the chain with the integrated potential weight. -> Trajectory gradient majorant.
- **step-bad-set-avoidance** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-bad-avoidance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-bad-avoidance): Bound the equilibrium mass of a Hamming neighborhood, use entropy to leave it with fixed mass, and concentrate the normalized distance. -> Uniform deterministic-time bad-set avoidance after fixed burn-in.
- **step-occupation-propagation** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-dyn-occupation-propagation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-dyn-occupation-propagation): Integrate avoidance, split large occupation events, and retain the crude potential only on their small probability. -> Logarithmic-horizon gradient propagation with superpolynomial error.
- **step-linear-concentration** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-linear-concentration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-linear-concentration): Insert the constant terminal gradient of a linear observable into propagation and then apply jump moments and the equilibrium gap. -> Uniform transient and stationary linear concentration.
- **step-median-scale** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-mixing-scale) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-mixing-scale): Use positive spin correlation to choose a separating linear statistic and entropy decay for the upper scale. -> Logarithmic median scale and exact crossing.
- **step-common-mass** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-common-mass) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-common-mass): Compare both means with the mean of the normalized common part. -> Mean discrepancy bound.
- **step-post-overlap-fields** [claim](#stmt-rcut-lem-cutoff-field-tails) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-lem-cutoff-field-tails): Bound field means by common mass and apply uniform centered exponential moments with a coordinate union bound. -> Superpolynomial deterministic-time field tails.
- **step-positive-lag** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-positive-lag) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-positive-lag): Compare early martingale energy with every late energy, average over the late interval, and compare the smoothed means using common mass. -> Mixing after every positive logarithmic lag.
- **step-restricted-continuous-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-rcut-thm-continuous-cutoff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-thm-continuous-cutoff): Apply positive-lag smoothing at the median and exclude premature common mass by contradiction with the first crossing. -> Uniform continuous cutoff around the median.
- **step-restricted-discrete-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-rcut-prop-discrete-cutoff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-discrete-cutoff): Verify fixed holding and every shifted Poisson average, then use the common clock lemma. -> Uniform discrete cutoff in attempted updates.
- **step-restricted-cutoff-ratio** [claim](#stmt-rcut-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rcut-prop-discrete-cutoff-2): Bracket the discrete mixing times by the cutoff sides and retain integer-rounding control before returning to disorder probability. -> Independent restricted-temperature mixing-time ratio theorem.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-euclidean-oscillation**: The oscillation of a real cube observable is bounded by the cube diameter times its largest Euclidean half-difference norm.
- **invariant-half-difference-convention**: A coordinate half-difference compares the observable with that spin fixed to its opposite signs and is independent of the original value of that spin.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-finite-check-as-cutoff-proof**: Treat passing finite-table checks as a certificate of the main asymptotic cutoff theorem. -> The finite checks establish the oscillation inequality only on their checked rational tables. They do not establish disorder convergence, the limiting operator, or logarithmic-time gradient propagation.
- **anti-use-explicit-temperature-only-schedule**: Replace the implicit equilibrium rate by its displayed upper bound to obtain an exact sampling schedule. -> An upper bound on the rate does not identify the rate that determines the cutoff location.
- **anti-use-changing-temperature-or-fields**: Extend the main cutoff location to changing temperatures or externally biased spin systems. -> Those settings are outside the stated cutoff mandate, even though some auxiliary estimates allow fields.
- **anti-use-confusing-update-clocks**: Use the continuous-time cutoff location as a count of attempted single-site updates. -> The clocks have different normalizations, and retained-spin attempts belong to the discrete kernel.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The finite cube oscillation bound admits exhaustive exact evaluation on rational observable tables. This executable certificate addresses that finite auxiliary result only. The proof extends the observable multilinearly, bounds its gradient by Jensen’s inequality, and integrates along a segment between vertices; the asymptotic cutoff theorem is outside the executable certificate.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON containing n and values; vertex indices encode spins by bits.
# PRECONDITIONS: n is an integer from 1 through 8; values contains exactly 2**n rational strings.
# OUTPUTS: Exact rational strings for oscillation_squared, gradient_squared, bound, and a boolean valid.
# TIME: Exhaustive enumeration of vertices and coordinate half-differences.
# SPACE: Stores the input table and scalar extrema.
# ARITHMETIC: Arbitrary-precision integers and exact rational arithmetic.
# FAILURE: Invalid input raises an exception; a false inequality sets valid to false.
import json
import sys
from fractions import Fraction

def solve(payload):
    n = payload['n']
    if type(n) is not int or not 1 <= n <= 8:
        raise ValueError('invalid dimension')
    raw = payload['values']
    if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(raw) != (1 << n):
        raise ValueError('invalid table size')
    if not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in raw):
        raise ValueError('rational strings required')
    values = [Fraction(item) for item in raw]
    gradient_squared = Fraction(0)
    for vertex in range(1 << n):
        energy = Fraction(0)
        for i in range(n):
            bit = 1 << i
            difference = (values[vertex | bit] - values[vertex & ~bit]) / 2
            energy += difference * difference
        gradient_squared = max(gradient_squared, energy)
    oscillation = max(values) - min(values)
    oscillation_squared = oscillation * oscillation
    bound = 4 * n * gradient_squared
    return {'oscillation_squared': str(oscillation_squared),
            'gradient_squared': str(gradient_squared),
            'bound': str(bound),
            'valid': oscillation_squared <= bound}

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(json.dumps(solve(json.load(sys.stdin)), sort_keys=True))
```

    "reason": "The finite cube oscillation bound admits exhaustive exact evaluation on rational observable tables. This executable certificate addresses that finite auxiliary result only. The proof extends the observable multilinearly, bounds its gradient by Jensen’s inequality, and integrates along a segment between vertices; the asymptotic cutoff theorem is outside the executable certificate.",
    "reference_code": "# INPUTS: JSON containing n and values; vertex indices encode spins by bits.\n# PRECONDITIONS: n is an integer from 1 through 8; values contains exactly 2**n rational strings.\n# OUTPUTS: Exact rational strings for oscillation_squared, gradient_squared, bound, and a boolean valid.\n# TIME: Exhaustive enumeration of vertices and coordinate half-differences.\n# SPACE: Stores the input table and scalar extrema.\n# ARITHMETIC: Arbitrary-precision integers and exact rational arithmetic.\n# FAILURE: Invalid input raises an exception; a false inequality sets valid to false.\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom fractions import Fraction\n\ndef solve(payload):\n    n = payload['n']\n    if type(n) is not int or not 1 <= n <= 8:\n        raise ValueError('invalid dimension')\n    raw = payload['values']\n    if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(raw) != (1 << n):\n        raise ValueError('invalid table size')\n    if not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in raw):\n        raise ValueError('rational strings required')\n    values = [Fraction(item) for item in raw]\n    gradient_squared = Fraction(0)\n    for vertex in range(1 << n):\n        energy = Fraction(0)\n        for i in range(n):\n            bit = 1 << i\n            difference = (values[vertex | bit] - values[vertex & ~bit]) / 2\n            energy += difference * difference\n        gradient_squared = max(gradient_squared, energy)\n    oscillation = max(values) - min(values)\n    oscillation_squared = oscillation * oscillation\n    bound = 4 * n * gradient_squared\n    return {'oscillation_squared': str(oscillation_squared),\n            'gradient_squared': str(gradient_squared),\n            'bound': str(bound),\n            'valid': oscillation_squared <= bound}\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    print(json.dumps(solve(json.load(sys.stdin)), sort_keys=True))\n",
    "test_vectors": [

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | A sampler can implement the stated conditional spin refresh and count attempted updates consistently with the discrete cutoff theorem. The implicit equilibrium rate and asymptotic disorder guarantee do not provide a calibrated stopping rule for a particular finite instance. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The finite path simulations approximate bounded smooth empirical tests through successive limits. They do not furnish a general game simulation engine or a finite-resolution accuracy contract for arbitrary trajectories. |
| tools | True | strong | implementable | inferred | The scalar certificate supplies a concrete construction for an interval calculator that encloses the specified finite quadrature sums using directed integer arithmetic and explicit transcendental remainders. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The frozen-field construction gives a concrete sampling algorithm for each conditional mesh endpoint: coordinates refresh independently using fields computed at the beginning of the bin. Its comparison with the original dynamics has a prescribed order of limits. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The recipe completions and visible exact spaces organize limiting observables in Hilbert spaces. They do not specify a finite storage representation with retrieval, update, or memory guarantees. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The model fixes ideal rate-one-per-site dynamics and uniformly selected single-site attempts. No accelerator construction or correspondence between these clocks and physical execution latency is established. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The projected row likelihood theorem controls moments under deterministic masks and integrated mask families. It supplies no adversarial security construction and explicitly excludes choosing a worst mask after observing the disorder. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The main sampling result assumes Gaussian disorder and zero external field. It does not construct a training procedure or establish cutoff for learned couplings and biases. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The scalar variational bound is an analytic certificate over a normalized function class. It does not construct an optimizer for a supplied combinatorial objective or justify a cooling schedule. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Conditional path trees attach independent branches at a shared state under specified Markov laws. This mathematical copying construction provides no distributed protocol, communication model, or fault-handling contract. |
| other | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | For statistical physics, the deterministic visible operator characterizes asymptotic relaxation through an equilibrium spectral construction. A separate finite experimental prediction or calibrated measurement procedure is ABSENT. |

          "anchor": "stmt-thm-row-projected-moments",

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-subcritical-temperature** (hypothesis): The cutoff theorem fixes the inverse temperature before the dimension limit. Critical temperatures, low temperatures, and dimension-dependent approaches to criticality are outside its conclusion. Blocked use: ['Apply the logarithmic cutoff location along a cooling schedule.', 'Claim a uniform cutoff theorem as temperature approaches the phase boundary.']
- **limit-gaussian-zero-field-model** (hypothesis): The main cutoff guarantee concerns symmetric zero-diagonal Gaussian interactions and zero external field. It does not certify arbitrary deterministic, sparse, non-Gaussian, or learned interactions. Blocked use: ['Transfer the cutoff theorem to a supplied graph optimization instance.', 'Assert cutoff for a trained biased spin model without a separate argument.']
- **limit-disorder-probability** (formal_scope): Convergence in probability over disorder is an asymptotic ensemble guarantee. It does not certify an accuracy threshold for an individually supplied finite interaction matrix. Blocked use: ['Treat every finite disorder realization as certified to mix at the asymptotic location.', 'Replace convergence in disorder probability by an almost-sure assertion.']
- **limit-implicit-cutoff-rate** (nonconstructive): The equilibrium rate remains implicit. Its displayed upper bound is not an equality and cannot supply an exact numerical stopping schedule by substitution. Blocked use: ['Identify the cutoff rate with the spin-edge upper bound.', 'Derive a calibrated finite sampling budget solely from the temperature.']
- **limit-cutoff-window-absent** (unknown): A cutoff window is ABSENT from the established conclusions. Blocked use: ['Publish an additive transition-window width or a finite-size error bar as a consequence of the main theorem.']
- **limit-attempt-clock-normalization** (formal_scope): The discrete clock counts uniformly selected refresh attempts, including outcomes that retain the old spin. Its cutoff location cannot be used unchanged for per-site continuous time or for a clock counting successful flips. Blocked use: ['Count only actual spin changes while applying the attempt-clock cutoff.', 'Interpret attempted updates as device wall-clock time.']
- **limit-imported-gap-field-uniformity** (hypothesis): The imported full-phase equilibrium gap is a zero-field input. Uniform external-field gaps require the additional observation construction or the restricted-temperature auxiliary argument. Blocked use: ['Apply the imported gap theorem directly at arbitrary external fields throughout the full phase.', 'Replace the posterior and cavity arguments by the zero-field gap alone.']
- **limit-stable-field-mean-diagnostics** (hypothesis): The arbitrary-law mean bound requires the deterministic diagnostics and stable-field implication. An arbitrary interaction matrix and field are insufficient. Blocked use: ['Use the mean-displacement estimate after checking only an equilibrium gap.', 'Omit the finite-word and stability margins in a changed-law comparison.']
- **limit-posterior-exceptional-paths** (hypothesis): The posterior and cavity gap assertions permit an exponentially rare ordinary observation failure. Their stopping rule is independent of the test, and a changed input law requires its own entropy comparison. Blocked use: ['Assume every observation path retains the posterior gap.', 'Transfer the ordinary exponential failure probability unchanged to an arbitrary tilted law.']
- **limit-fixed-burn-in-density** (formal_scope): The specific density estimate fixes burn-in before taking the dimension limit. It does not assert a quenched estimate uniform at logarithmic burn-in times. Blocked use: ['Insert a dimension-dependent logarithmic time directly into the fixed-time density estimate.', 'Assign an unstated convergence rate to its fixed-time limit.']
- **limit-causal-single-endpoint-trees** (hypothesis): Admissible path trees use actual conditional copies attached at a single endpoint, fixed horizons, polynomial weights, and the prescribed initial density bound. Blocked use: ['Attach a new branch conditioned on both endpoints.', 'Replace the permitted weighted tree laws by arbitrary entropy-small path tilts.']
- **limit-mesh-and-truncation-order** (approximation): Frozen-field simulation comparisons require the stated successive dimension, truncation, mesh, and smoothing limits. Empirical agreement supplies no uniform finite-mesh trajectory certificate. Blocked use: ['Claim a finite-resolution total-variation guarantee from empirical simulation convergence.', 'Choose approximation parameters depending on dimension without proving the required uniformity.']
- **limit-tracial-versus-operator-error** (approximation): Spatial square-mean approximation does not make diagonal matrices close in operator norm. Rare coordinate types retain their base actions in the word representation. Blocked use: ['Discard a diagonal solely because its support has vanishing spatial proportion.', 'Multiply a tracial approximation error by an arbitrary correlated localized vector as though the error were operator-small.']
- **limit-admitted-query-algebra** (hypothesis): Mixed-slot bounds alone do not establish opened derivative closure. Query edges, propagation edges, and coefficient labels must belong to the admitted path algebra with its entry predictions. Blocked use: ['Extend the opened-network conclusion to arbitrary bounded-operator query maps.', 'Infer conditional derivative control from separate first-slot Jacobian estimates alone.']
- **limit-one-tree-representation** (formal_scope): The hidden-word representation is constructed for the fixed finite tree. Compatible choices across different trees are not asserted. Blocked use: ['Combine independently selected creation representations at different endpoints without a joint construction.']
- **limit-independent-root-history-class** (formal_scope): Independent-root factorization is restricted to spin, field, and bounded likelihood histories. It does not extend to arbitrary noncentered recipes or recipes sharing site seeds. Blocked use: ['Assume independent limiting site laws for arbitrary shared-seed calculations.', 'Factor noncentered Gaussian queries using the independent-root history theorem.']
- **limit-deterministic-integrated-masks** (formal_scope): Projected likelihood moments allow deterministic masks and integrated deterministic mask families. They do not provide a simultaneous bound for a disorder-selected worst mask. Blocked use: ['Optimize a mask after observing the disorder and invoke the projected moment bound.', 'Replace an integrated exceptional-mass estimate by a supremum over auxiliary parameters.']
- **limit-negative-likelihood-moments** (edge_case): Negative projected moment orders refer to the unrestricted positive likelihood. A likelihood multiplied by a cutoff indicator may vanish and is not covered by that inverse-moment assertion. Blocked use: ['Apply an inverse-moment estimate to a restricted label that can be zero.']
- **limit-hidden-propagation-terminal-exactness** (hypothesis): Hidden propagation requires squared-contraction hiddenness at the initial endpoint, an exact terminal gradient, bounded endpoint moments, polynomial envelopes, and the stated weighted terminal derivative budget. Blocked use: ['Apply hidden propagation to an arbitrary terminal vector field.', 'Substitute weak Hilbert-space orthogonality for the required squared-contraction condition.', 'Remove the terminal derivative budget without another proof.']
- **limit-bilinear-averaging-only** (formal_scope): Endpoint averaging is an equivalence in the specified hidden bilinear tests. It is not an operator-norm replacement of arbitrary path labels by predictors. Blocked use: ['Replace every path label by an endpoint predictor in an unrestricted operator norm estimate.']
- **limit-weighted-embedding-direction** (formal_scope): The ordinary and weighted completions have a continuous injective forward embedding. Weighted approximation need not imply ordinary approximation, and the inverse embedding need not be bounded. Blocked use: ['Invert the embedding to obtain unweighted decay directly from weighted decay.', 'Identify the weighted vector norm with the separate derivative form.']
- **limit-selected-good-times** (formal_scope): Comparison times are selected from integrated budgets after extraction. Their existence does not establish that every prescribed interior time or a worst auxiliary time satisfies those budgets. Blocked use: ['Replace selected comparison times by a supremum over all interior times.', 'Differentiate rough random scalar coefficients when testing vector exactness.']
- **limit-no-defect-approximant-scope** (hypothesis): The no-defect bound requires own-spin-independent polynomially bounded vector fields on the posterior-gap disorder events. Its negligible stopping remainder is taken separately for each fixed approximant. Blocked use: ['Apply the bound to an unbounded dimension-dependent approximation family without uniform stopping control.', 'Omit own-spin projection when the vector components depend on their own spin.']
- **limit-uniform-block-effectivity** (nonconstructive): Uniform block contraction supplies existence of fixed block and burn-in constants after choosing the required envelopes and accuracy. It supplies no quantitative rate for a fixed-time limiting error. Blocked use: ['Read explicit numerical block lengths or burn-in constants from the existential argument.', 'Iterate nonuniform fixed-time errors before establishing the common block event.']
- **limit-slow-visible-preparation-order** (hypothesis): The slower-visible lower bound requires an isolated slow eigenspace, a common trajectory Poincaré bound, coefficient alignment, admissible prepared laws, and the prescribed order of coarse recipes, block length, fine recipes, and preparation time. Blocked use: ['Apply the spin-edge lower observable when a slower visible mode determines the rate.', 'Refine preparation recipes while silently reusing derivative constants chosen for a different calculation.', 'Use an arbitrary initial-law perturbation in place of the constructed preparation.']
- **limit-restricted-auxiliary-uniformities** (formal_scope): The independent appendix cutoff argument and its field-uniform auxiliary estimates belong to the restricted-temperature regime. The main full-phase theorem does not extend those auxiliary uniformities throughout the phase. Blocked use: ['Claim a field-uniform full-phase cutoff theorem from the appendix gap bound.', 'Apply the restricted gap constant outside its positive-temperature margin.']
- **limit-scalar-certificate-function-class** (hypothesis): The scalar variational certificate requires the stated Gaussian field law, temperature interval, square-integrable function class, nonnegative residual function, and normalization. Blocked use: ['Apply the scalar margin to an arbitrary empirical field distribution.', 'Use the bound on unnormalized functions without the corresponding homogeneous rescaling.']
- **limit-scalar-arithmetic-versus-integrals** (approximation): Finite scalar sums require analytic quadrature and tail bounds, outward arithmetic, normalization and standard-deviation transfer, and replacement of the mean parameters before they certify the continuous moments. Blocked use: ['Treat approximate finite-sum centers as certified continuous expectations.', 'Replace outward enclosures by ordinary floating-point agreement.', 'Treat verification of the scalar arithmetic as verification of the full cutoff theorem.']
- **limit-deterministic-time-avoidance** (formal_scope): Bad-state avoidance and local-field tails are uniform at deterministic observation times. They do not assert a simultaneous good-field event along every trajectory time. Blocked use: ['Interpret small marginal bad-state probabilities as a bound on ever visiting the bad set.', 'Take a trajectory-time maximum using a deterministic-time field-tail estimate without additional control.']
- **limit-clock-transfer-preconditions** (hypothesis): The binomial clock transfer requires bounded arrays, a fixed thinning parameter, diverging clock size, and convergence of every fixed shifted Poisson average. The upper cutoff transfer also verifies a uniform holding bound. Blocked use: ['Infer discrete upper cutoff from unshifted Poisson convergence alone.', 'Apply the clock comparison to an unbounded observable array or a changing thinning parameter without a new argument.']
- **limit-finite-oscillation-certificate** (formal_scope): Exact rational-table checks can certify the oscillation calculation on their supplied inputs. They do not decide the universally quantified real-observable lemma or the asymptotic disorder-dependent cutoff theorem. Blocked use: ['Promote a finite-table oracle receipt to a proof of the full cutoff theorem.', 'Treat agreement on selected rational tables as exhaustive coverage of every real observable.']

Corpus status: formalized in the source corpus (toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1`, Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`). Not re-checked here; the statements give the exact quantifiers and hypotheses, not a proof.

Scope note of family 227 (`lean/docs/227.md`, verbatim):

> The following describes the scope of the Lean formalization related to the following accompanying paper(s):
>
> - [A spectral gap throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase](../../preprints/A-spectral-gap-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/main.pdf)
> - [Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase](../../preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)
> - [Critical slowing down in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model](../../preprints/Critical-slowing-down-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)
> - [Stretched-exponential barriers for typical SK initial states](../../preprints/Stretched-exponential-barriers-for-typical-SK-initial-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)
>
> ## Scope
>
> For every fixed inverse temperature $0<\beta<1$, the formalization proves a dimension-independent Poincaré inequality for the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with probability tending to one over the disorder. Equivalently, the unscaled single-site heat-bath spectral gap stays bounded away from zero. For dynamics that choose one site uniformly at each discrete step, the spectral gap is at least $1/(Cn)$ with probability tending to one, for a constant $C$ depending on $\beta$.
>
> The formalized supporting result proves ratio cutoff for discrete single-site heat-bath dynamics in the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model for $0\le\beta<1/2$. For every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and $\eta>0$, the probability over the disorder that $t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)/t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1-\varepsilon)>1+\eta$ tends to zero as $n\to\infty$. The denominator is positive for all sufficiently large sizes.
>
> The paper's full range $\beta<1$, explicit cutoff location, and continuous-time conclusion are outside this selected statement.
>
> At criticality in the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model, the formalization proves that for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the continuous-time mixing time lies between $n^{2/3-\varepsilon}$ and $e^{\varepsilon n}$, and the discrete-time mixing count lies between $n^{5/3-\varepsilon}$ and $e^{\varepsilon n}$, with probability tending to one over the Gaussian disorder. The disorder has independent off-diagonal entries of variance $1/n$. Continuous updates have rate one per site; discrete time counts uniformly chosen single-site update attempts. Mixing is worst-start total variation at threshold $1/4$, with holding allowed.
>
> For deterministic times $t_n=o(n^{2/3})$ or update counts $k_n=o(n^{5/3})$, the Gibbs mass of realized starting states still farther than $1/4$ from equilibrium tends to one in probability. For every deterministic positive sequence $M_n\to\infty$, the covariance operator norm and the linear Rayleigh supremum, using the unscaled heat-bath Dirichlet form, both lie between $n^{2/3}/M_n$ and $M_n n^{2/3}$ with probability tending to one. The covariance result does not give an upper bound for the full inverse spectral gap.
>
> The formalization proves a stretched-exponential mixing obstruction for the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$. At time $\exp(n^{1/10000})$, the expected Gibbs mass of initial configurations whose total-variation distance from equilibrium exceeds $1/4$ tends to one. Since this mass lies in $[0,1]$, it also tends to one in probability over the disorder.
>
> The result covers both rate-one-per-site continuous-time heat-bath dynamics and the same stated number of discrete update attempts.

```lean
import Mathlib

namespace OAI

noncomputable section
open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter

namespace SKGap

abbrev Spin (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Bool
abbrev Edge (n : ℕ) := {p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2}
abbrev Disorder (n : ℕ) := Edge n → ℝ

def spinValue (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

def coupling {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (i k : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  if h : i < k then g ⟨(i, k), h⟩ else
    if h : k < i then g ⟨(k, i), h⟩ else 0

def hamiltonian {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (x : Spin n) : ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ i, ∑ k, spinValue (x i) * coupling g i k * spinValue (x k) +
    ∑ i, h i * spinValue (x i)

def weight {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (x : Spin n) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (hamiltonian g h x)

def partition {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x, weight g h x

def mass {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (x : Spin n) : ℝ :=
  weight g h x / partition g h

def expectation {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (f : Spin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x, mass g h x * f x

def variance {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (f : Spin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  expectation g h (fun x => (f x - expectation g h f) ^ 2)

def flip {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) (x : Spin n) : Spin n :=
  Function.update x i (!(x i))

/-- Conditional expectation under the actual Gibbs law given all other spins. -/
def conditionalExpectation {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ)
    (i : Fin n) (f : Spin n → ℝ) (x : Spin n) : ℝ :=
  (weight g h x * f x + weight g h (flip i x) * f (flip i x)) /
    (weight g h x + weight g h (flip i x))

/-- Unscaled form: each site has a rate-one clock. -/
def dirichlet {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) (h : Fin n → ℝ) (f : Spin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, expectation g h (fun x => (f x - conditionalExpectation g h i f x) ^ 2)

def disorderLaw (β : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Measure (Disorder n) :=
  Measure.pi (fun _ : Edge n => gaussianReal 0 (Real.toNNReal (β ^ 2 / n)))

def poincareEvent (n : ℕ) (C : ℝ) : Set (Disorder n) :=
  {g | ∀ f : Spin n → ℝ, variance g 0 f ≤ C * dirichlet g 0 f}

/-- Rayleigh quotient definition of the uniform-site discrete heat-bath gap. -/
def discreteGap {n : ℕ} (g : Disorder n) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ f : Spin n → ℝ, 0 < variance g 0 f ∧
    r = dirichlet g 0 f / ((n : ℝ) * variance g 0 f)}

def MainStatement (β : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => disorderLaw β n (poincareEvent n C)) atTop (nhds 1) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => disorderLaw β n {g | 1 / (C * (n : ℝ)) ≤ discreteGap g})
      atTop (nhds 1)

theorem sk_main (β : ℝ) (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβ1 : β < 1) : MainStatement β := by
  sorry

end SKGap
end

end OAI
```

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove worst-case total-variation cutoff for the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick heat-bath dynamics at every fixed inverse temperature $`0\leq\beta\lt 1`$. With rate-one refresh at each spin, the cutoff location is $`\log n/(2\lambda(\beta))`$ for a positive deterministic rate $`\lambda(\beta)`$. The location for uniformly chosen single-site update attempts is <i>n</i> times as large. Convergence is in probability over the disorder.
